sentences.text: Facts of the case in brief is that the appellants/claimants filed a claim application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ( for short MV Act) claiming compensation on account of death of one Sugulu Ram in an accident which took place on 07.05.2014.

As per the pleadings of the claim application deceased Sugulu Ram went in a baraat to village Barang and while returning along with his maternal uncle Cheta Ram, near the Mudkona turning, he got down and was going by walk, at that point of time, the offending vehicle tractor bearing registration No. CG 14-MC-1960 driven rashly and negligently by respondent No.1 driver hit the deceased as a result of which the tractor lost balance and turned turtle, on account of which he sustained grievous injury on the head and died on the spot.
Therefore appellants/claimants claimed total compensation of Rs.15,20,000/-.

3. The respondent No.1/owner-driver filed a written statement and denied the pleadings of the claim application and submitted that he had valid and effective driving license and the vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 Insurance Company and therefore if any liability is found the same shall be fastened upon the Insurance Company to make the payment.
4.

The respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed its written statement and submitted that though the offending vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company as per terms and conditions of the policy, however the offending vehicle was used for baraat on hire and reward and the offending vehicle was insured for agricultural purpose, therefore there is a violation of the Insurance Policy thus, the claim against the Insurance Company may be rejected.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, learned Tribunal has framed as many as four issues.
Issue No.1 & 2 is with regard to happening of the accident on account of rash and negligent driving by respondent No.1/driver- owner causing death of the deceased was decided as proved.
Issue No.3 to Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:22967 5 was also decided in favour of the claimants.
However the Insurance Company was exonerated from paying the compensation.

6. Shri Kesarwani, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the learned tribunal has not awarded just compensation as the income of the deceased was not taken as pleaded and the future prospects and other heads has not been paid properly.
Even if the Insurance Company has been exonerated, the learned Tribunal ought to have passed an order of pay and recover.

7. Shri Rastogi, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal with regard to the exoneration of the Insurance Company has not been challenged by the respondent No.1/ driver-owner and the award passed is just and proper and does not require any interference.
8. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

Learned Tribunal has found the income of the deceased to be Rs. 3,000/- per month and after deducting 1/3 rd income for his personal expenses, assessed his income to Rs. 24,000/- applying the multiplier of 12 looking to the age of the deceased and awarding Rs. 1,00,000/- as loss of consortium and Rs. 25,000/- for funeral expenses awarded total compensation of Rs. 4,13,000/-.
The income assessed by the learned Tribunal is on the lower side, the date of accident is 07.05.2014

2 and considering the nature of work and the pleadings and the minimum wages, the notional monthly income of the deceased would safely be taken as 5,500/-.

Since the deceased was found to be aged about 47 years, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pranay Sethi & others (2017) 16 SCC 680 25% future prospect is added to the income of the deceased.

11. At this stage, I shall consider whether there can be an order passed under the doctrine of "pay and recover".

12. This Court keeping in view the benevolent object of the MV Act and other relevant factors arising in the case, hereby issues the direction against the Insurance Company to pay the total awarded compensation to the appellants/claimants first and then to recover the said sum from the insured by applying the principle of "pay and recover".

In this regard I am guided by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Manuara Khatun & Ors Vs. Rajesh Kr. Singh & Ors (2017) 4 SCC 796 and Balu Krishna Chavan vs Reliance General Insurance Company Limited, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932.
